The toolbox is closely tied to the programme's capacity-building work. The **[Stock Monitoring Tool](smt.qmd)** on the iMarine gateway is the main training environment: trainees run methods there without programming, and use the toolbox pages for the method's data needs, assumptions, diagnostics and misuse risks. The apps lower the entry barrier; the catalogue pages are what keep their results interpretable.

| Training element | Apps | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Length-based assessment | SMT: TropFishR, LBI, LBSPR; FLicc module | Live; FLicc prototype in development |
| Surplus production models | SMT: SPiCT, JABBA, CMSY | Live; CMSY temporarily unavailable |
| Data preparation | FishualizeR | Live |
| Mixed fisheries and harvest strategies | mmsyFM Shiny app | Runs locally; iMarine hosting under consideration |
| Assessment to management (participatory) | FPAT workbook and FPAT App | R package runs locally; hosted app to be confirmed |

## Methods and where to run them

```{r}
#| echo: false
source("R/toolbox.R")
m <- read_methods()
m <- m[m$category == "Assessment" | m$app != "", ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Method = link_name(m, "../"), Category = m$category,
                        `In R` = m$software, `No-code app` = ifelse(m$app == "", "–", m$app),
                        check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE, escape = FALSE)
```

## From assessment to management: FPAT workshops

FAO Technical Paper 737 describes two linked workshops, each about three days, tested in West Africa, Indonesia and Latin America.

| Workshop | Participants | Sequence |
|---|---|---|
| **Fishery performance assessment** | 3–12 each of harvesters, post-harvest representatives and managers, plus scientists | Review pre-scored [FPI and governance metrics](../methods/empirical/fpi.qmd) by sector → share and compare with reference fisheries → agree 3–8 outcomes to improve → identify actions and the enabling conditions they change |
| **FPAT App / MSE** | 4–12 scientists and technical managers | Population dynamics basics → app overview → agree the input data → agree feasible measures → historical reconstruction and projections → compare options against the agreed outcomes → try alternative datasets → assign responsibility for a management plan and data collection |

Lessons from the pilots that apply to any toolbox training:

- Agree the basic terms (*stock*, *population*, *fishery*, *fishing effort*) first, in a dedicated session or pre-reading.
- A slide overview, then a live demonstration on a case study, then hands-on work in small groups. One-to-one work on the participants' own data teaches more than presentations about data.
- Start the MSE session from a summary of the current management system for each stock (size limits, closures, catch limits).
- Taking part in a workshop does not by itself build the capacity to lead one; train facilitators separately.

## From training to assessment

Apps are well suited to learning a method and to first screening of a stock. Before results are used for advice, the analysis should meet the same standard as a scripted one:

- the [data preparation](../data-tools/data-preparation.qmd) steps have been done on the real data;
- the method's **misuse prevention** checks pass;
- the [diagnostics](../guidance/diagnostics.qmd) and [sensitivity runs](../guidance/sensitivity.qmd) are reported;
- the settings and data are saved, so that the run can be repeated, ideally as an R script.
